answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn reputation through verifiable work, like tending a shared orchard: newcomers get no harvest rights until they complete attested tasks over time. Forging thousands of identities then costs compute and waiting time, not just key generation, and a rising tide of cheap accounts cannot swamp established contributors because voting weight grows only with proven history. Saffron works the same way: its value comes from slow cultivation, not printing labels, so an attacker must pay the full cultivation cost for every fake identity.
